name: Farside
label: Revelation
lede: An Orange County band that once had Zack de la Rocha on second guitar, turned down the majors when punk went gold, and quit after three albums rather than become a nostalgia act.

eras.title: Borrowed gear and a future rap-metal star
eras.text: Farside came out of the late-'80s Orange County straight edge scene alongside Inside Out and Sense Field. For a stretch their second guitarist was a University High kid named Zack de la Rocha, who left before they recorded an album and started Rage Against the Machine.

years.h: Popeye Vogelsang asks for a tryout and Farside is born
years.p: Rob Haworth, bassist Josh Stanton and drummer Bob Beshear have a band; Michael "Popeye" Vogelsang asks to try out and ends up singing and playing guitar.

years.h: Zack de la Rocha plays second guitar in Farside
years.p: Zack de la Rocha, also singing in [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], plays second lead guitar in Farside in 1990–91. He never makes a Farside album, but he is on the early demos later collected on Scrap.
years.xp: De la Rocha went to University High in Irvine, the same school scene Farside came from. By late 1991 he was fronting Rage Against the Machine, and Popeye told OC Weekly in 1999 that having Zack in the band had been an enjoyable experience, and that success like his definitely changes your life.

yt: How Farside became a Revelation band
years.h: Rochambeau, Farside's Revelation debut, cut on Christmas Day
years.p: Recorded at For The Record Studios on Christmas Day with equipment borrowed from friends. Popeye wrote just one of its songs, Worlds. Trouser Press heard acoustic guitars and songs about unity and the personal as political.

eras.title: Louder, thicker, and not for sale
eras.text: With Kevin Murphy writing alongside Popeye, Farside got heavier and better. Then the Offspring and Green Day made Southern California punk a gold rush, and Farside said no to the people holding the checkbooks.

years.h: Kevin Murphy goes from touring guitarist to full member
years.p: Kevin Murphy fills in on tour, then joins Farside full time in 1993, replacing Rob Haworth. From here Murphy and Popeye Vogelsang write the songs together.
Producer Jim Monroe pushes the band louder and thicker. Popeye says the title came from gear held together with bubblegum and rubber bands.
years.xp: The line-up is Popeye Vogelsang, Kevin Murphy, bassist Bryan Chu and drummer Bob Beshear. Trouser Press heard twin guitars that gnarl forcefully and melodies with a Hüsker Dü streak, from the punk rush of Square One to a melancholy closer.

years.big: Offers came in. Farside stayed on Revelation.
q: We have total creative control and can do whatever the fuck we want to.
years.h: Farside turn down major labels during the 1994 punk boom
years.p: When the 1994 punk boom sent labels hunting through Orange County, Farside passed on major-label offers, OC Weekly reported, and stayed with Huntington Beach's Revelation Records.
years.xp: The members went to college and built careers instead. By 1999 Popeye was editing an employee newsletter in Los Angeles by day.

years.h: Scrap gathers Farside's early demos, Zack de la Rocha included
years.p: A compilation of early recordings, including demos from the line-up with Zack de la Rocha on second guitar.

years.h: Farside's European tour: a rented van and a run of mishaps
years.p: Behind Rigged, Farside take a rented van around Europe. Popeye told Dying Scene the tour was one mishap after another; it was also the band's last real tour for four years.

years.h: The self-titled Farside EP, a bridge to the last album
years.p: Six songs on Revelation. Popeye has said it wasn't anyone's favorite release.

eras.title: Named for the engineer, made as a goodbye
eras.text: Farside went quiet for years while the members built lives. They came back to make one more record, knowing it would be their last, and spent more than they had making it.

years.h: The Monroe Doctrine, named for engineer Jim Monroe
years.p: Farside's third album, made as a farewell and over budget. OC Weekly counted acoustic ballads, grindcore, speed-metal riffs and a cover of Graham Parker's Blue Highway.

years.h: Bassist Bryan Chu leaves to teach kindergarten
years.p: Bryan Chu marries, moves to San Francisco and becomes a kindergarten teacher, OC Weekly reported. Sean "Rosey" Rosenthal, 21, takes over on bass.

years.h: Farside hit the East Coast with Fastbreak and Save the Day
years.p: Farside's first tour since 1995 runs up the East Coast with Fastbreak and Save the Day.

years.h: Live at the Melody Bar, New Brunswick NJ, August 3, 1999
yt: Live at the Melody Bar, New Brunswick NJ, August 3, 1999

years.h: Farside play a final tour and break up
years.p: After eleven years, three albums and two EPs, Farside split after one last tour. Popeye has said the breakup was mutual.

eras.title: No reunion, but no silence
eras.text: Farside never played again, and Popeye has said he has no interest in trying. The songs kept turning up anyway: in a snowboarding game, on anniversary vinyl, and in a new Popeye band back on Revelation.

years.h: Seven Day Constant lands in a snowboarding video game
years.p: Farside's Seven Day Constant is on the soundtrack of Amped: Freestyle Snowboarding. Popeye starts Your Favorite Trainwreck with [[Jeff Caudill|6a41fff4-9b5c-4b1c-9ebf-4df434fdbbec]] of [[Gameface|c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27]].
By 2010 Popeye had spent three years doing professional voice-over work for animation, commercials and video games, he told Dying Scene.

q: I've always been super proud of Farside's tenure with Revelation.
years.h: Popeye's new band [[Calling Hours|a76e3280-2524-461d-855f-0550ebedff93]] releases Say Less on Revelation
years.p: Popeye Vogelsang sings over four members of [[Don't Sleep|0f073ffb-b2de-4017-9646-bf80a73079ec]]; [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] of [[Battery|172d89ba-95ab-4e30-92a2-fe836ba0601e]] produces. McTernan and Judge's [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] steered the demos to Jordan Cooper.
Revelation reissues Rigged on mint green eco-vinyl with a 16-page booklet, plus new color pressings of Rochambeau and The Monroe Doctrine. Still no reunion shows.
